title: Ephemeral context eviction strategy (scratchpad)
body:
Purpose:
- quick notes + exploratory designs for ephemeral per-session context eviction for local/edge sessions (users/ folder brain dump).
- goal: keep tail latency low while bounding memory usage for many concurrent sessions on a single worker.

Constraints / assumptions:
- sessions have variable token budgets (some long-lived chat, some bursty QA).
- model runtime holds KV cache in GPU memory where possible; falling back to compressed CPU store or disk.
- some prefixes are high-value (system prompts, recent user conversation), others are cheap to recompute or rehydrate.
- we must avoid catastrophic quality regressions when evicting (i.e., don't evict the system prompt unless explicit).

Goals / metrics:
- mem_per_worker <= configured cap (e.g., 48GB GPU / worker).
- P99 latency increase due to eviction < 5% for typical chat workload.
- cache_miss_rehydrate_time < 200ms for hot rehydrates (prefetched).
- track quality_delta_by_evict (small prompt sets to detect degeneration).

Eviction policy palette (brainstorm):
1) TTL + token-count caps (simple)
   - each session gets token_budget (configurable by tier), TTL since last active.
   - evict sessions idle > TTL or when total_tokens > cluster_budget.
   - pro: simple. con: not adaptive to importance.

2) Weighted LRU (LRU with weights by importance)
   - weight(session) = base + recent_activity*alpha + pinned_flag*inf + recency_boost
   - eviction sorts by weight ascending.
   - need a cheap estimate: store last_n_token_count, last_active_ts, pinned boolean.

3) Prefix-preserving partial eviction (shrink from tail)
   - keep first K tokens (system prompt + recent N tokens), evict middle older chunks but preserve prefix.
   - idea: store context as circular segments: [prefix | core | tail]. Evict core segments first.
   - useful to prevent losing system prompt and immediate recency.

4) Semantic compaction / summarization
   - when session goes cold, run lightweight summarizer (or call hosted summarize endpoint) to compress history into a short synthetic summary chunk. Keep summary in cache instead of full tokens.
   - tradeoff: compute cost and possible hallucination; good for long chats.

5) Hot-cold tiering + background rehydrate queue
   - hot sessions remain in GPU; cold sessions moved to compressed CPU store or paged to disk. On access, background rehydrate attempts to prefetch top-K sessions predicted to be accessed next.
   - prediction model could be simple heuristic (recent activity, user tier) or ML-based.

6) Token-coalescing and shared common prefixes
   - if multiple sessions share identical system prompts or identical initial prefixes, store a shared read-only prefix cache and reference it, minimizing duplication.

API / config sketch (rough):
- SessionManager config (yaml-like):
  eviction_policy: "weighted-lru"  # options: ttl, weighted-lru, prefix-preserve, semantic-compact, tiered
  total_token_budget_per_worker: 1200000
  default_session_token_budget: 8192
  min_prefix_keep_tokens: 128
  cold_store: {type: "compressed-heap", path: "/mnt/cache"}
  rehydrate_prefetch: {enabled: true, lookahead: 16, background_worker_count: 2}
  summarizer: {enabled: true, model: "small-summarizer-v1", max_tokens: 128}
  eviction_hook: "/internal/session/evict-hook"

- Minimal endpoints (sketch):
  POST /session/create -> {session_id, token_budget?}  // note: create can accept pin/prefetch hint
  POST /session/pin -> {session_id, reason}  // disables eviction for pinned items
  POST /session/peek -> {session_id, window=256} -> streaming small chunk without full rehydrate
  POST /session/evict -> {session_id, force=true|false}  // exposed for admin / debug
  POST /session/summarize -> async request to generate compressed summary

ASCII diagram (rough):

  client ---> session-manager ---> runtime (GPU KV cache)
                 |                       |
                 |                       --> cold-store (compressed CPU / disk)
                 |
                 --> rehydrate-queue (background) --> runtime

Notes on storage model:
- store per-session KV in segments: metadata (head pointers), prefix_segment (immutable), active_segment (mutable, GPU hot), archive_segments (compressed).
- each segment has token_count, compressed_size, checksum.
- implement quick heuristics to estimate rehydrate cost = compressed_size / io_bandwidth + decompress_time + copy_to_gpu. Use as eviction cost estimate.

Rehydration flow (sketch):
- on first token request for a cold session -> respond with ephemeral placeholder if model supports streaming? otherwise block until rehydrate.
- better: return partial continuity by streaming from a summary + then rehydrate full context in background and patch KV cache once ready. Caller may get a signal (event) when full context is available.

Observability signals to add:
- gauge: sessions_in_gpu, sessions_in_cold, sessions_pinned
- histogram: rehydrate_latency, evicted_tokens, eviction_trigger_reason (manual/ttl/memory)
- alert: sustained_rehydrate_rate > threshold -> indicates under-provisioned memory or bad policy

Quality guardrails:
- never evict segments marked mandatory (system prompt, safety info).
- add per-session tests: generate reference replies for a small eval prompt set before/after eviction policy to detect drift. Store eval score changes in a time-series.

Open questions / TODOs:
- how to represent "importance" cheaply across millions of sessions? propose: 8-bit importance score updated on activity, decayed exponentially.
- should summarization be local (edge) or call hosted summarizer? latency vs quality tradeoff.
- exact serialization format for compressed segments (zstd + vector-quantized embeddings?).
- eviction interactions with model kv cache format (some models require absolute contiguous KV vs chunkable frames). Need runtime API to allow chunked imports.
- policy for multi-tenant workers: per-customer quotas vs global worker quotas.

Immediate next steps:
- spike: implement weighted-lru skeleton + TTL fallback in dev branch. Measure memory vs P95 latency on small cluster with mixed chat/qa workload. (owner: me)
- prototype prefix-preserve: implement segment-trimming API and a test harness to assert system prompt persistence. (owner: Liam)
- draft a minimal session-manager config proposal for product to review (owners: me + Priya).

Quick todo list:
- [ ] write integration test harness for rehydrate_latency
- [ ] add metric events for eviction_reason
- [ ] benchmark summarizer cost vs compression ratio
- [ ] add a small CLI tool to inspect session segments on a worker (for debugging)

Random notes / heuristics (brain dump):
- keep ~128 tokens of prefix by default; recent 512 tokens are cheap to keep for responsiveness; older content can be compressed aggressively.
- for conversational agents with tool use, prefer to keep tool-call history intact (can't lose it) — treat it as pinned.
- offer customer-level knobs: aggressive (best-effort), conservative (preserve quality), premium (larger hot budget).

End of scratchpad.

Notes to self: when I revisit, add concrete benchmark numbers from the 2025-inference-bench run and link GH PRs.
